title: What is space complexity, and how much stack space does recursion use?
description: Auxiliary space versus input space, and why a recursion depth of n costs O(n) stack.

title: How should you approach a DSA problem in a coding interview?
description: A repeatable framework: clarify, examples, brute force, optimise, code, test.

title: How do merge sort and quicksort work?
description: Divide and conquer two ways: merge after splitting versus partition before recursing.

title: How do you search a sorted 2D matrix?
description: Treat a fully sorted matrix as one array, or walk from the top-right corner of a row-and-column sorted one.

title: What is the prefix sum technique?
description: Precompute running totals so any range sum is one subtraction.

title: How do you check if a string is a valid palindrome?
description: Two pointers from both ends, skipping non-alphanumeric characters and ignoring case.

title: How do you design a min stack with O(1) getMin?
description: Keep the running minimum alongside each pushed value.

title: How do you find the next greater element for every item (Daily Temperatures)?
description: A decreasing stack of indices answers next-greater queries in one pass.

title: How do you find the largest rectangle in a histogram?
description: An increasing stack finds each bar's left and right limits in O(n).

title: How do you find the longest common prefix of an array of strings?
description: Vertical scanning, horizontal reduction, or sort and compare the first and last word.

title: How does the KMP string-matching algorithm work?
description: The prefix (failure) function lets the search never move backwards in the text.

title: What is the fast and slow pointer technique?
description: Two pointers at different speeds find middles, cycles and k-th-from-end nodes.

title: How do you invert a binary tree?
description: Swap left and right children at every node, recursively or with a queue.

title: What is a segment tree and when do you need one?
description: Range sums or minimums with point updates, both in O(log n).

title: What is a graph, and how do you represent it?
description: Adjacency list versus adjacency matrix versus edge list, and when each fits.

title: How do you solve the Rotting Oranges problem with multi-source BFS?
description: Start BFS from every rotten orange at once and count the levels.

title: How do you find strongly connected components in a directed graph?
description: Kosaraju's two DFS passes and Tarjan's low-link values.

title: How does the Floyd-Warshall algorithm work?
description: All-pairs shortest paths by allowing one more intermediate vertex at a time.

title: How do you find the cheapest flight with at most K stops?
description: Bellman-Ford limited to K+1 rounds, or BFS by stops.

title: How do you solve the Jump Game?
description: Track the farthest reachable index in one pass.

title: How do you solve the Gas Station problem?
description: If total gas covers total cost, the start is right after the lowest running balance.

title: What is bitmask dynamic programming?
description: Encode a subset as an integer so DP can range over subsets, as in the travelling salesman problem.

title: How do you generate all subsets of an array?
description: Include-or-exclude recursion, iterative doubling, or bitmasks.

title: How do you generate all permutations of an array?
description: Swap-based or used-array backtracking, and handling duplicates.

title: How do you solve the Combination Sum problem?
description: Backtracking with reuse allowed and pruning once the sum overshoots.

title: How do you solve the N-Queens problem?
description: Place one queen per row and track used columns and diagonals.

title: What are the most useful bit manipulation tricks for interviews?
description: Masks, x & (x - 1), x & -x, XOR identities and shifts.
